capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Roruka or Vitabhaya/Vitibhaya'; Roruka 'corresponds to the mediaeval Arohr and the modern-day Rohri' (Sindhu-Sauvira page); the Aror page gives 27.65N 68.98E and calls Roruka 'capital of the Sauvira Kingdom'. The page does not date the seat; the span is the state's life.

correction.text: 'its southern border being the Indian Ocean and its northern border being the Punjab around Multan': Sindhu, 'the inland area between the Indus River and the Sulaiman Mountains', and Sauvira, 'the coastal part of the kingdom' (Sindh and the Multan country)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; sa-01-a listed Sindhu-Sauvira as a state without one). The infobox gives no area; the shape resolves to about 208,000 km2 from the page's bounds, the Indian Ocean in the south and 'the Punjab around Multan' in the north. The Sindhu and Sauvira halves are not separated; the epics treat them as two kingdoms (Sindhu Kingdom page: 'two warring states').

region.text: 'its southern border being the Indian Ocean and its northern border being the Punjab around Multan': Sindhu, 'the inland area between the Indus River and the Sulaiman Mountains', and Sauvira, 'the coastal part of the kingdom' (Sindh and the Multan country)

ledger.note: c. 1000 BCE: the kingdom of Sindhu and Sauvira stands on the lower Indus. Infobox 'Established: c. 1000 BCE', 'Iron Age India'. The page names the bounds, not a founding event; the Sauvira and Sindhu pages (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauvira_Kingdom, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sindhu_Kingdom) give only legendary founders, sons of Sivi, and no dates.

wars.name: Achaemenid conquest of the Indus Valley

zones.text: the lower Indus from Multan to the sea

wars.outcome: Persian victory: 'In 518 BCE, Sindhu-Sauvira was conquered by the Persian Achaemenid Empire under Darius I'; the land becomes the satrapy of Hindush.
wars.note: The Hindush dossier carries the wider war (535-518) from the conquest page. The Sindhu-Sauvira page names no battle; its ruler 'during the 6th to 5th centuries BCE' was 'a powerful king named Udayana'.

certainty.note: A kingdom known from the epics and Buddhist texts; only its bounds (the sea and Multan) are given, and the page dates only its start (c. 1000) and its conquest (518).

notes: Written because the Hindush infobox names Sindhu-Sauvira as its predecessor and sa-01-a asked for it (its Gandhara notes: 'Sindhu-Sauvira (a belligerent of the conquest) has no row'). The sa-01 convention of -600 for the janapadas is not applied: the page's own start is c. 1000 BCE, and the epics make the state older still, so the -1000 start is the infobox's 'c.' date with the whole life soft. No dated event between 1000 and 518 BCE is on the three pages; the Sindhu and Sauvira halves may have been separate kingdoms before the Pali texts join them. After the Persian conquest the page's Mousikanos (capital Roruka, met by Alexander 'in 326 BCE') belongs to the Macedonian-era lower Indus, which this batch draws as Hindush's last years. Gazetteer: Rohri/Aror (27.65N 68.98E) is not a place; Sukkur is the nearest gazetteer name.
